name: ns_proofsearch_null_profile_cap
rubric_version_reason: Branch-killer substrate: target one obligation (NullProfileCapped) for one named class, NOT the global Track B theorem. Per advisor_channel Turn 10 §4.
description: NS Track B branch-killer: null-profile cap. Closes either by Lean instantiation of NullProfileCapped on a named class, or by deterministic Python falsifier exhibiting a null profile with payoff > price.

cage_meta.class_reason: Qualitative theorem-search over a named obligation in a fixed Lean kernel; not numerical curve fitting.

theorem_packet_contract.reason: Branch-killer substrate. The candidate must name the null class, expose its construction, expose the declared kernel terms, and produce a theorem (positive arm) or a falsifier (negative arm). The pre-judge gate enforces these top-level functions before paid judge calls.

disable_evidence_fit_gate_reason: The target is a proof-shaped predicate instantiation, not data fitting.
disable_uniqueness_gap_gate_reason: The hard gate evaluates Lean closure or Python falsifier directly.
persona: You are a ruthless NS Track B null-profile-cap referee. Reward only ONE of two outcomes: (A) a Lean instantiation of NullProfileCapped for an explicit named null class (shear, Beltrami, embedded Euler, or a fixed Leray-invisible family) on the flat torus under the declared pricing kernel from ns_pricing_kernel_limit_passage.lean; or (B) a deterministic Python audit exhibiting a null profile with payoff > price under that same declared kernel. Penalize: any global Track B claim from null-class evidence, any new pricing-kernel definition not shown equivalent to the declared one, any sorry-laden Lean proof, any backward fitting of the kernel to the profile, any restatement of the obligation without an instantiation, any conflation with concentration/dichotomy/cross-profile/vanishing branches. The substrate is BRANCH-LOCAL by design.

dimensions.name: Null Class Naming
dimensions.description: Does the candidate name an explicit null class (shear, Beltrami, embedded Euler, or a fixed Leray-invisible family) BEFORE evaluating the cap?

dimensions.name: Pricing-Kernel Consistency
dimensions.description: Does the candidate use the declared kernel from ns_pricing_kernel_limit_passage.lean, with no silent redefinition?

dimensions.name: Predicate Instantiation
dimensions.description: Does the candidate produce a Lean instantiation of NullProfileCapped for the named class, OR a deterministic Python falsifier with concrete (price, payoff, selfTax) values?

dimensions.name: Class Coverage
dimensions.description: Does the candidate cover the entire named class, not just one mode? (E.g. all shear vector fields, not just one f(y).)

dimensions.name: Anti-Tautology Discipline
dimensions.description: Does the candidate avoid backward fitting the kernel to the profile, defining 'null' as 'the set where the cap holds', and similar circular moves?

dimensions.name: Scope Honesty
dimensions.description: Does the candidate label its result as a per-class branch closure, not a global Track B theorem? Does it explicitly NOT cite concentration/dichotomy/cross-profile/vanishing branches as load-bearing?

dimensions.name: Generative Yield
dimensions.description: Does the candidate produce a usable Lean theorem, a precise Python falsifier with output JSON, a named obstruction, or a sharper boundary between null classes?

dimensions.name: Nonclaim And Resource Safety
dimensions.description: Does the candidate avoid Clay/global-NS overclaim, packet hunting, and unbounded computation?

dimensions.name: Lean Discipline
dimensions.description: If positive arm: does the Lean proof avoid `sorry`, import the declared kernel, and not redefine its types?

criteria.Null_Class_Naming: Full credit requires a named class declared at the top of the candidate, with the construction exposed before the cap is evaluated.
criteria.Pricing_Kernel_Consistency: Full credit requires using PricingProfile and the kernel as declared; any modification must be explicitly justified and shown equivalent.
criteria.Predicate_Instantiation: Full credit requires a Lean theorem of the form `theorem null_profile_cap_concrete (P : PricingProfile) (h : P.isNull) (...) : ProfileNoArbitrage P` for the named class, OR a Python script that constructs P with isNull=True and payoff > price under the declared kernel.
criteria.Class_Coverage: Full credit requires the proof or falsifier to cover the full named class. A single-mode check is insufficient.
criteria.Anti_Tautology_Discipline: Full credit requires no backward kernel fitting; the kernel and class must be declared first, the cap evaluated second.
criteria.Scope_Honesty: Full credit requires the substrate output to label its result as 'branch-closure for class X' not 'Track B closed'.
criteria.Generative_Yield: Full credit requires either a Lean theorem (positive arm), a deterministic falsifier (negative arm), a named obstruction (e.g. 'Beltrami needs a separate kernel'), or a sharper class boundary.
criteria.Nonclaim_And_Resource_Safety: Full credit requires no Clay or global-NS claim, no packet hunt, no unbounded dense computation.
criteria.Lean_Discipline: Full credit requires the Lean proof to compile, import the declared kernel, and not contain `sorry`.

success_criteria: Names the null class explicitly (one of shear, Beltrami, embedded Euler, named Leray-invisible family).
Exposes the construction of the named class as a top-level function.
Uses the declared pricing kernel from ns_pricing_kernel_limit_passage.lean without redefinition.
Produces either a Lean instantiation of NullProfileCapped for the class OR a Python falsifier with concrete (price, payoff, selfTax).
Covers the entire named class, not a single mode.
Labels the result as a branch closure, not as global Track B closure.
failure_modes: Searching for new packet families instead of instantiating the predicate.
Defining a new pricing kernel and using it to satisfy the cap.
Defining 'null' as 'the set where the cap holds' (circular).
Single-mode checks instead of class-wide proof or falsifier.
Claiming global Track B from a null-class result.
Using degree-only q>p scaling without the exact quartic survival.
Backward fitting (price/payoff chosen to make the cap hold).
